gaps.evidence: The EQ-VT QC software checks interviewer performance and compliance with the interview script and produces daily QC evaluations and a final QC report; no quality-control software function value exists.
gaps.importance: Quality control software is central to the protocol 2.0 workflow reported here.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider adding a QUALITY_CONTROL software function value.
source: Methods > Data Collection and Quality Control Process

gaps.evidence: The six additional DCE tasks with duration and a death alternative are described as a methodological add-on whose data 'will be reported elsewhere'.
gaps.importance: The add-on data are collected in this study but no results are reported here.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Link results when the separate report is identified.
source: Methods > Valuation Interview and Methods of Eliciting Preferences

gaps.evidence: The paper reports that a multi-arm DCE with 3365 respondents and 19 designs 'was conducted', but refers to Mulhern [13] (doctoral dissertation, 2020) for design details and analyses only a subset of 8 designs (N = 1432), so the data may be reuse of a prior research collection.
gaps.importance: Determines whether the choice data are CURRENT_STUDY_COLLECTION or PRIOR_RESEARCH_COLLECTION.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer check of the relationship between this analysis and the parent multi-arm DCE reported in reference [13].

gaps.evidence: The paper reports a German sample recruited through a German panel but does not state the survey language.
gaps.importance: Language of administration is relevant for valuation studies and for instrument version identity.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave language null and confirm from the linked feasibility study or supplementary material.

gaps.evidence: Participants were 'recruited from Germany using an online panel ... for participation in a validation study [11]', while the retest was administered for the present reliability assessment; it is unclear whether the initial test data are current-study or prior-research collection.
gaps.importance: Determines whether the test wave should be treated as prior research collection with source-study context.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Confirm with the authors or reference [11] whether the test wave belongs to the same data collection as this reliability study.

gaps.evidence: The Genetic Algorithm was used for item selection and scale reduction (short-form item set derivation), which is neither plainly quantitative analysis nor mapping/derivation in the controlled list.
gaps.importance: Affects functional classification of the study's principal development method.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a method function for item selection or scale reduction; QUANTITATIVE_ANALYSIS used as the closest fit.
source: Methods > Statistical methods > Short Form Development

gaps.evidence: Participants completed a brief demographic questionnaire used only to describe participant characteristics (Table 1); no controlled instrument function covers background-characteristic collection.
gaps.importance: Low: affects only the characteristics questionnaire, not the studied instrument.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a controlled function for participant-characteristic or background measurement.

gaps.evidence: A stated aim was also to explore how feasible it is for proxies to rate residents' QoL using the EQ-HWB (Theme 1: feasibility/ability to proxy report), but no controlled purpose value covers feasibility of instrument completion.
gaps.importance: Medium: a co-equal reported aim and outcome family (FEASIBILITY) has no matching purpose value.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a FEASIBILITY_EVALUATION research purpose value.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports the analysed sample and the intended sample of around 30 participants but gives no counts for people approached, screened, or declining participation.
gaps.importance: Low: recruitment flow is not required for the qualitative findings.
gaps.proposed_resolution: None; source does not report recruitment flow counts.

gaps.evidence: Data were obtained from the recurring county public health survey 'Life & Health—young people' 2014, with microdata provided by Region Örebro County; results from the survey are reported elsewhere, so origin could be routine monitoring collection or prior research collection.
gaps.importance: Affects whether instrument and administration uses should be current activity or source-study/input provenance.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer to confirm whether the county monitoring survey counts as routine service collection or prior research collection.

gaps.evidence: ICD-11 was used to define the disease groups of the study samples; no method function fits a disease classification system used for grouping evidence.
gaps.importance: Low; affects only the classification of a grouping tool.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a classification-system function or record such standards as a separate entity type.
source: Methods: Assessment of the Preference-Based Measures (PBMs)

gaps.affected_key: handling of utility scores below 0 in the empirical validity analysis
gaps.evidence: The Methods section ends mid-sentence: 'There is a possibility that utility scores below 0 ... would be different for the EQ-5D-Y-5L and EQ-5D-Y-3L ... To overcome this,'
gaps.importance: The procedure underlying the reported sensitivity analysis (utilities restricted to 0–1) is not stated in the available text.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Check the published version or supplementary material for the completed sentence describing the handling of negative utility scores.
source: Methods > Utility score performance (empirical validity), final paragraph

gaps.evidence: Disability weights (WHO 2013, GBD 2013, Murray 1994) are applied to prevalent cases of vision impairment to derive DALYs, rather than to instrument responses, so the application of this reusable weight set does not fit ScoringUse.
gaps.importance: Affects representation of preference-based weights applied at population rather than respondent level.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider extending scoring application to population-level weight sets applied to prevalence estimates.
source: Methods > Definition and estimation of intangible effects

gaps.evidence: The study applies data visualization recommendations and techniques (and the Sankey Diagram) to create and modify the presentation of EQ-5D-5L data; no method_function value covers information visualization or presentation design.
gaps.importance: Central method of the study's development component
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a method function for data visualization or presentation design.

gaps.evidence: "Due to the purpose of this study and the trademark of the instrument, feedback on the EQ-5D-5L descriptive labels was not reported."
gaps.importance: Part of the collected feedback is not available in the publication
gaps.proposed_resolution: Note the withheld result component; no controlled value applies.

gaps.evidence: The principal contribution is explaining variation in the provision/utilization of a clinical intervention (peripheral nerve blocks) plus its association with clinical and service-use outcomes; both APPLIED_USE_RESEARCH (use/provision) and HEALTH_OUTCOME_RESEARCH could describe this study.
gaps.importance: Affects family-level aggregation of this non-EQ, EuroQol-funded applied study.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer confirmation whether provision/utilization of a clinical treatment falls under APPLIED_USE_RESEARCH in an instrument-focused ontology.

gaps.evidence: Subgroup analyses compared patient/study groups (age, design, timing), contexts (geographic region, income status) and EQ-5D instrument versions (3 L vs 5 L) within one meta-analysis, but only one comparison_structure value can be assigned.
gaps.importance: Affects how the review's comparative structure is represented; BETWEEN_GROUP, BETWEEN_CONTEXT and BETWEEN_INSTRUMENT are each partially applicable.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow multiple comparison_structure values or record secondary comparison axes for subgroup meta-analyses.
source: Results: Subgroup analysis of EQ-5D utility scores

gaps.evidence: The planned comparison is between two modes of administration (face-to-face vs videoconference) of the same cTTO method, which fits both BETWEEN_CONTEXT ('modes') and BETWEEN_METHOD.
gaps.importance: Affects how mode-of-administration comparisons are counted across the corpus.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Confirm whether administration-mode comparisons map to BETWEEN_CONTEXT or BETWEEN_METHOD.
source: Methods > Statistical Comparison between Modes of Administration

gaps.evidence: The paper reports interviews in Spain and Belgium but does not state the interview or instrument language.
gaps.importance: Limits language-level description of the two valuation data collections.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consult the national EQ-5D-Y-3L valuation study reports for language details.

gaps.evidence: The study compares directly reported versus recalled scores within the same person (WITHIN_PERSON) but also explicitly compares correspondence between the EQ-5D summary score and the EQ-VAS (a hypothesis-driven instrument comparison).
gaps.importance: Affects whether the comparison axis is recorded as within-person or between-instrument.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow a secondary comparison value or record BETWEEN_INSTRUMENT as an additional design axis value for planned instrument comparisons nested within a within-person design.

gaps.evidence: The Theoretical Framework of Acceptability is a conceptual framework applied analytically to map themes; it is recorded as a MethodUse with QUALITATIVE_ANALYSIS, but a named conceptual framework could alternatively be typed as a protocol or concept.
gaps.importance: Affects registry typing of a named framework used in analysis
gaps.proposed_resolution: Registry review of whether named conceptual analysis frameworks map to Method or Protocol identities

gaps.affected_key: software used for conditional logit estimation and bootstrap
gaps.evidence: Methods report conditional logit estimation and cluster bootstrap with percentile method but name no software; the discussion notes that no open-source software is available for kaizen-task DCEs.
gaps.importance: Limits reproducibility description of the analysis.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record software if reported in the supplementary technical file.

gaps.evidence: Some interviews occur before the main online data collection and some after initial analysis, interviews are conducted while respondents complete the survey, and focus groups discuss study findings; this fits both SEQUENTIAL and EMBEDDED.
gaps.importance: Affects how the mixed-method structure of the planned study is represented.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow more than one integration value or add a combined sequential-embedded value.

gaps.evidence: Data access and record linkage of survey responses to provincial administrative databases were provided by Population Data BC; no method function covers record linkage or data management.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a DATA_LINKAGE_OR_MANAGEMENT method function.
source: Methods: Study Design and Data Sources

gaps.evidence: The planned comparison is between nested prediction models (Base vs EQ-5D-5L-enhanced vs VR-12-enhanced) rather than between instruments per se, although the two PROMs distinguish the enhanced models.
gaps.importance: Affects how the comparison axis represents model-versus-model evaluation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a BETWEEN_MODEL comparison value or confirm BETWEEN_INSTRUMENT for predictor-set comparisons.

gaps.evidence: The single FACIT-COST item FT12 was used as an external anchor for test-retest and responsiveness analyses and was excluded from the total score, but no use type represents a single item within an instrument acting as an anchor.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow an item-level instrument component use or an explicit anchor function
source: Methods > Statistical analyses > Evaluation of changes in SFT status

gaps.evidence: The principal output is a reusable reporting checklist that governs how valuation-study methods are reported, which fits METHODS_RESEARCH (method or protocol quality) but could also be read as a conceptual classification of valuation-study components (CONCEPTUAL_FRAMEWORK_DEVELOPMENT).
gaps.importance: Affects the single primary family assignment for this study.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer confirmation of whether reporting-guideline development maps to METHODS_RESEARCH or CONCEPTUAL_FRAMEWORK_DEVELOPMENT.

gaps.evidence: The pre-existing checklist from the EQ-5D valuation review supplied the initial 35 items and was used to score published valuation studies for example selection; no listed product function (ANALYSIS_OBJECT, COMPARATOR, EVIDENCE_SYNTHESIS_TARGET) exactly describes this input role.
gaps.importance: Affects the recorded function of the predecessor checklist.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a product function for an input or predecessor product used to build a new product.

gaps.evidence: The article title states 'RETRACTED ARTICLE' but the supplied full text contains no retraction notice, date, or reason.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain the separate retraction notice record to supply date, asserting party, reason, and notice DOI.

gaps.evidence: The stated aim is usability, usefulness and acceptability testing of a decision aid before implementation; no controlled purpose value denotes usability or acceptability evaluation, so IMPLEMENTATION_EVALUATION was used as the closest fit.
gaps.importance: Medium - the principal scientific aim is only approximately represented

gaps.evidence: Clinicians assessed asthma control using GINA criteria; this is a clinician-rated observation rather than a participant response, qualitative material, aggregate estimate, model parameter, simulated unit, or document.

gaps.evidence: The Chinese Diagnosis and Treatment Protocol for COVID-19 (Trial Version 10) defines the disease severity classification and clinical recovery criteria used as external criteria, which is not a governing study, valuation, translation, quality-control, reporting or appraisal function.

gaps.evidence: The follow-up questionnaires are described as part of the ongoing LIS injury surveillance data collection ('LIS is an ongoing data collection in fourteen hospitals'; 'A stratified sample of patients received questionnaires 6 months and 12 months after trauma'), so the survey responses could be routine surveillance collection rather than collection designed for this study.
gaps.importance: Affects whether the analysis is primary or secondary use of survey data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Confirm with source authors whether the 2017 follow-up survey was designed for this psychometric study or is standard LIS follow-up.

gaps.importance: Determines whether the participant data are current-study collection or reuse of a prior research collection.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Source review of reference [6] to confirm whether the December 2018 survey is a separate prior study collection.

gaps.evidence: 'conducted the sessions after completing four pilot interviews' - no participant characteristics, sampling, or results are reported for the pilot stage.
gaps.importance: Prevents linking pilot interviews to a population and separating pilot from formal data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Keep the pilot part with the interview count only; do not attribute pilot participants to the formal samples.

gaps.evidence: The stated aim is to co-design (create) the implementation of EQ-5D-Y-5L in routine care, producing the P-PROM ROCK Program; the vocabulary offers IMPLEMENTATION_EVALUATION (evaluating implementation) but no value for participatory design or development of an implementation program.
gaps.importance: Affects the primary purpose classification of a co-design study whose principal output is an implementation program.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider adding an IMPLEMENTATION_DESIGN or PROGRAM_CO_DESIGN research purpose value.

gaps.evidence: The defining planned comparison is between the newly developed Chinese lay QoL framework and the existing EQ-HWB conceptual framework, which is neither a between-group, between-instrument, nor between-method comparison of study units.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider an instrument function for use of item content as a deductive coding frame.

gaps.evidence: Google reCAPTCHA v3 was implemented across four interactions to flag bot responses; its role is quality control of collected data, but the software_function vocabulary has no quality-control value.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a paradata/process-data level value; DOCUMENT used as nearest available.

gaps.evidence: The source describes data as 'routinely collected by the UK MS Register', which is itself described as a prospective, longitudinal, observational cohort study, and the limitations refer to 'use of pre-existing datasets'.
gaps.importance: Determines whether registry PROM data map to PRIOR_RESEARCH_COLLECTION or ROUTINE_SERVICE_COLLECTION.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer confirmation of the preferred origin value for research-registry cohort data.
source: Methods — UK MS register and population

gaps.evidence: The paper reports multinational European and US study centres but does not state the languages of the EQ-5D-3L or other questionnaires administered.
gaps.importance: Language versions matter for pooled multinational EQ-5D data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave language fields null until the source cohorts report them.

gaps.evidence: The CVP sample was restricted to exclude respondents preferring a community setting or no vaccination card, but the resulting analysed sample size is not reported.
gaps.importance: Prevents an exact analysed denominator for the CVP kaizen results.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Request the analysed CVP subsample size from the authors or primary publications.

gaps.evidence: The COSMIN study design checklist is used as the conceptual framework for the components analysed (relevance, comprehension, comprehensiveness) and for deductive coding, rather than clearly governing the whole study or guiding critical appraisal.
gaps.importance: Affects whether COSMIN is represented as a governing protocol, an appraisal protocol, or an analysis framework.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Review whether a framework-for-analysis protocol function is needed.

gaps.evidence: The acknowledgements thank the QUOKKA project Caregiver Consumer Advisory Group, but no activity, stage, or influence on the study is reported.
gaps.importance: Consumer advisory involvement may have shaped the study but cannot be modelled without a reported activity and influence.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave unmodelled unless the source reports the activity and its influence.

gaps.importance: Low: affects only the function label of one supporting method use.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer to confirm the appropriate method function for a priori expert consensus hypothesis setting in psychometric validation.

gaps.evidence: The study is a scoping review conducted per JBI guidance with thematic and narrative synthesis; the vocabulary offers SYSTEMATIC_REVIEW, META_ANALYSIS or NARRATIVE_SYNTHESIS but no exact 'scoping review' value.
gaps.importance: Affects accurate classification of the synthesis design for review-type studies.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a SCOPING_REVIEW value or reviewer confirmation that NARRATIVE_SYNTHESIS is the intended mapping.

gaps.evidence: The paper states that members of the general population took part in beta-testing and piloting of the survey instrument but reports no number of beta testers or pilot respondents.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain the beta-testing and pilot participant counts from online supplemental appendix 1 or the authors.
source: Methods and analysis/Patient and public involvement

gaps.evidence: Preference evidence from the existing 2013 US EQ-5D-Y-3L value set was used to select coma comparison profiles and rank improvements for the experimental design, which is neither an analysis object, comparator, nor evidence-synthesis target.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a product function such as DESIGN_INPUT for an existing product used to construct an experimental design.
source: Methods and analysis/Experimental design/Generating the Y-3L profiles...

gaps.evidence: The protocol mixes past tense for design steps ('A two-stage sampling design was used'; power analysis carried out) with future tense for fieldwork ('The survey will be conducted four times over 2023 and 2024'), published July 2024, so whether data collection is active or not yet started is ambiguous.
gaps.importance: Affects the reported execution state of the planned longitudinal survey.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Confirm the fieldwork start date with the authors or a later report before fixing the execution state.
source: Abstract, Methods and analysis; Sampling strategy; Survey design

gaps.evidence: The study tests whether EQ-TIPS-5L severity concords with preferences and whether attribute levels influence choices; this is preference-based assessment of the descriptive system that could map to CONTENT_TEST_OBJECT (relevance of levels) or MEASUREMENT_PROPERTY_TEST_OBJECT (level-ordering validity).

gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer decision on whether preference-based level-ordering and redundancy assessment counts as content testing or measurement-property testing.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer adjudication between the protocol-demonstration/method-comparison reading and the descriptive-system property-assessment reading.

gaps.evidence: The focus groups are described only as '2 focus groups' with a topic guide; mode, setting, language, and dates are not reported.
gaps.importance: Limits characterization of the qualitative face validity component.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave channel, setting, language, and time point empty until the source reports them.
source: Methods > Bolt-on Dimension Selection and Development

gaps.evidence: The sample size formula of Casagrande, Pike, and Smith determines the number of respondents per health state pair; it could map to SAMPLING or to EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN.
gaps.importance: Affects method-function counts for power and design procedures.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Review whether power/sample-size calculation should have its own method function.

gaps.evidence: The reusable output is a DCE experimental design (150 pairs in 10 blocks) later adopted by the international EQ-5D-Y-3L valuation protocol; no product_type value covers an experimental design.

gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider an EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN product type value.

gaps.evidence: The study compares conventional versus retrospective change within the same person, but also explicitly hypothesizes and compares agreement between the EQ-5D-3 L summary score and the EQ-VAS ('Agreement ... as measured with EQ-VAS, is lower compared to the agreement if HRQL was measured with EQ-5D-3 L') and compares the recall and then-test methods.
gaps.importance: Affects whether the comparison axis is WITHIN_PERSON, BETWEEN_INSTRUMENT or BETWEEN_METHOD.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow multiple resolved comparison values on one axis, or confirm WITHIN_PERSON as the governing structure with instrument comparison recorded elsewhere.

gaps.evidence: 'This study utilizes data from a registry-based study on injury patients ... the Brabant Injury Outcome Surveillance (BIOS) study' but 'Response shift items and recall questions were intentionally included in the 3 month follow-up survey'.
gaps.importance: Determines whether the questionnaire data are CURRENT_STUDY_COLLECTION or PRIOR_RESEARCH_COLLECTION.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Confirm with the authors whether the recall/then-test module constitutes current-study collection embedded in an ongoing cohort.

gaps.evidence: 'Parents provided clinical data for the patients and filled in the proxy version of EQ-5D-Y. The EQ-5D-Y proxy report is discussed elsewhere.'
gaps.importance: The proxy data component was collected in this study but no results are reported in this publication.

gaps.evidence: "They were all trained at Umeå University in January 2020 following the standard training protocol provided by the EuroQol group."

gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a training-protocol function value or explicit guidance for interviewer training protocols.

gaps.evidence: The paper describes face-to-face computer-assisted personal interviews following the EQ-VT interviewer script but does not state the interview or instrument language.
gaps.importance: Language of administration is relevant for a valuation study conducted in a non-standard EQ-VT setting.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave language fields null and flag as not reported.

gaps.evidence: The source states only that each interviewer completed at least two sets of 5 pilot interviews, without a total pilot interview count.
gaps.importance: Prevents an exact pilot-stage sample count separate from the main data collection.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record the pilot phase as a study part without an exact sample size.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports interviews with German caregivers in Germany but does not state the language of the EQ-HWB-9 version or of the interviews.
gaps.importance: Language version is relevant for face validity of an instrument used in a non-source-language setting.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave language fields empty pending author clarification.
source: Methods > Structure of the interview guide

gaps.evidence: The study combines a planned comparison of EQ-5D-5L, EQ-HWB, EQ-HWB-9 and BIT (between-instrument), known-groups comparisons by sweating and weather adaptation (between-group), and within-person score change across waves (within-person), but only one comparison value can be recorded per axis.
gaps.importance: Affects faithful representation of the study's comparison structure
gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow multiple comparison_structure values for one study or part, or add a secondary comparison axis.

gaps.evidence: The paper states that patients were administered the HSCL-25 followed by the EQ-5D-3L at the beginning of residential treatment, but does not state the administration channel (paper, electronic, or other).
gaps.importance: Affects comparability with the general population sample, which used postal and web modes.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave channel empty for the patient sample administration.
source: Methods > Outcome measures > Hopkins symptom checklist

gaps.affected_key: mean age of the SUD patient sample
gaps.evidence: Methods report mean age 23.9 years (SD = 3) while Results report mean 23.8 years (SD 3.2) for the same 178 patients.
gaps.importance: Minor descriptive inconsistency in sample characteristics.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record both reported values without repair if a conflict item is preferred.

gaps.evidence: Gazepoint GP3 binocular video-based system, 60Hz, 0.5–1 degrees precision, positioned 65 cm from the respondent and 40 cm below eye level.
gaps.importance: The specific eye-tracking hardware and its precision determine the feasibility findings and the exclusion of glasses-wearing respondents, but no entity type records measurement hardware.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add a device or apparatus use type, or an explicit hardware field on MethodUse.

gaps.evidence: A pilot study with 50 participants was performed to test the data collection procedures and evaluate the traditional Chinese version of the EQ-VT program, but no quantitative pilot results are reported beyond respondent comments referenced in the discussion.
gaps.importance: Prevents linking pilot outcomes to the design changes made before the formal study.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record pilot outcomes if reported in a companion source.

gaps.evidence: The PTO method is itself an object of investigation (how participants interpret PTO tasks and whether the questions capture relative weights), but the method_function vocabulary offers no value for a method examined as a study object; PREFERENCE_ELICITATION was retained with CURRENT_STUDY_OBJECT context.
gaps.importance: Affects retrieval of studies that evaluate a preference elicitation method's comprehension and performance.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a method function for a method under evaluation, or guidance that CURRENT_STUDY_OBJECT context plus the elicitation function is the intended pattern.
source: Section 3.2.1 Challenges for participants in responding to PTO questions

gaps.evidence: Interviews were 'transcribed using automated intelligent verbatim transcription' but the transcription software is not named.
gaps.importance: Prevents recording the transcription tool used for the qualitative data.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave unrecorded unless the software is identified in supplementary material.

gaps.evidence: The Canadian time trade-off-derived EQ-5D-5L value set is cited only as an example scoring algorithm in the narrative; it is neither an analysis object, comparator, nor evidence-synthesis target.
gaps.importance: Prevents accurate representation of a value set that is only referenced in a conceptual article.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a REFERENCE_ONLY product function for products mentioned without an analytic role.
source: Section: EQ-5D DESCRIPTION, USES, CONVERSION TO HEALTH-UTILITY AND QALYS

gaps.evidence: Interviews were conducted in the Netherlands with Dutch respondents, but the source does not state the instrument or interview language.
gaps.importance: Language of administration is relevant for valuation studies and for reuse of the elicited utilities.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave language fields empty unless the authors report the language.
source: Section 4.1 Sample and data collection strategy

gaps.evidence: The sample was recruited using a 'door-knock' approach, but the number of households or individuals approached, and the participation rate, are not reported.
gaps.importance: Limits assessment of selection and representativeness of the pilot sample.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record approached and eligible counts if reported in supplementary material or a related report.
source: Methods > Sample and administration of survey, para 3

gaps.evidence: The study compares four valuation methods (between-method) and, within the same respondents, two perspectives (within-person), but the axis permits only one value.
gaps.importance: medium
gaps.proposed_resolution: Permit a secondary comparison value or an explicit within-person comparison alongside the between-method comparison.

gaps.evidence: The study simultaneously compares patient versus caregiver reports (within dyad), the same rater at two time points (within person), and the Y-3L versus the Y-5L instruments (between instrument), but only one comparison value can be recorded on the axis.
gaps.importance: Recording only WITHIN_DYAD omits the planned instrument comparison and the within-person test–retest structure.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Permit multiple comparison_structure values for one study or add an explicit secondary comparison key.

gaps.evidence: The EQ-VT QC software assessed interviewers' performance and compliance and produced QC reports used for exclusion decisions; no quality-control software function exists in the vocabulary.
gaps.importance: Quality-control software is central to EQ-VT valuation studies and is currently forced into DATA_MANAGEMENT.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider adding a QUALITY_CONTROL software function.
source: Methods > Data collection and quality control process

gaps.evidence: The interview included 'a country-specific questionnaire' with no description of its content or analytic role.
gaps.importance: Its function in the study cannot be determined from the source.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Confirm the instrument content and function from the linked study protocol.
source: Methods > Data collection and quality control process

gaps.evidence: The paper does not state the language of the instruments or interviews, although interviews were conducted in Romania.
gaps.importance: Language is a standard administration fact for valuation studies.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Retrieve language details from the study protocol publication.
source: Methods > Data collection and quality control process

gaps.evidence: Known-group analyses in Table 6 report group totals summing to 112 rather than the 117 completers, without an explanation of the difference.
gaps.importance: Affects the analysed denominator for discriminatory power findings.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Seek an author-reported analysis sample size for the known-group comparisons.

gaps.evidence: The sociodemographic questionnaire collected age, sex, backpack weight perception, sports participation and family relationship, which were only described in Table 1 and not analysed as predictors or outcomes.
gaps.importance: Low: affects only the descriptive covariate instrument, not the measurement-property results.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a controlled function for descriptive background or covariate collection instruments.

gaps.evidence: The paper states that codes for analysis are available upon reasonable request but does not name any analysis software or package.
gaps.importance: low
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record software use if a named program is identified in supplementary material.

gaps.evidence: The WVS/EVS merging protocol governs data construction, but no controlled protocol function covers data merging or dataset construction.
gaps.importance: Medium: the merging protocol defines the analysed dataset.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a data-construction or data-management protocol function.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports multilevel mixed models and regressions but names no statistical software.
gaps.importance: Low: analysis software is not required for interpretation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave software absent unless a later source reports it.

gaps.evidence: The modified faces ('smiley') scale from the UK Household Longitudinal Study was used by 8–10-year-olds to rate the severity of candidate labels, which is neither current health measurement nor scoring of an EQ instrument.
gaps.importance: Affects how rating-scale tools used to judge instrument wording are classified.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider an instrument function for a rating scale used as a severity-judgement response format in instrument development.

gaps.evidence: The review of existing HRQoL instruments and dictionaries generated candidate labels rather than identifying evidence for synthesis; EVIDENCE_IDENTIFICATION is the closest available function.
gaps.importance: Affects counting of document-review methods used for instrument content generation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a method function for documentary item or label generation in instrument development.

gaps.evidence: The EuroQol Quality Control tool version 2.5 flags anomalous interviews and generates daily QC reports; no software function value describes quality control.
gaps.importance: Quality-control software is central to EQ-VT valuation fieldwork across the corpus.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider adding a QUALITY_CONTROL software function value.

gaps.evidence: The interviewer training protocol governs interviewer training rather than quality control, valuation or reporting; QUALITY_CONTROL_PROTOCOL is the nearest fit.
gaps.importance: Interviewer training protocols are a recurring EQ-VT component.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a training-protocol function value or confirm mapping to QUALITY_CONTROL_PROTOCOL.

gaps.evidence: The paper states it 'harnessed data from the US EQ-5D-5L face-to-face valuation study and the US EQ-5D-5L online valuation experimental study', but only the face-to-face study has a separate citation (ref 19), so the online arm could be current-study collection rather than prior research collection.
gaps.importance: Determines whether the online valuation data are current-study or prior-research collection and whether related instrument, software, and administration uses are direct current or source-study activity.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Confirm from the cited source study whether the online experimental valuation arm was conducted as part of the present investigation.

gaps.evidence: Structured metadata gives article_type 'editorial' and category 'Commentary', while the text presents a derived set of 22 criteria as a conceptual output.
gaps.importance: Affects whether the publication form is CONCEPTUAL_ARTICLE or OPINION_ARTICLE.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer confirms form against journal section labelling and article content.

gaps.evidence: The Methods section describes search, screening and extraction but reports no critical appraisal / risk-of-bias protocol and no reporting guideline (e.g. PRISMA) for the review.
gaps.importance: Limits assessment of the methodological quality control of this systematic review.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record absence of a critical-appraisal protocol and reporting guideline for this review.

gaps.evidence: Participants were probed to consider Canadian HTA guidelines on health valuation, which act as normative decision guidance rather than a study, valuation, translation, quality-control, reporting, or appraisal protocol.
gaps.importance: Affects representation of the HTA guidance that shaped participants' reasoning about the source of preferences.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add a protocol function for reimbursement or HTA methods guidance.
source: Results > Source of health state preferences, paragraph 2

gaps.evidence: The reported outcomes are stakeholders' normative and methodological views (who should value child health, from which perspective, and with which method), which fit neither preference/utility nor a conceptual classification family exactly.
gaps.importance: Affects outcome-family aggregation for stakeholder-engagement studies.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider an outcome family for stakeholder views or normative method preferences.
source: Results > Source of health state preferences

gaps.evidence: The paper reports descriptive, correlation, effect-size and internal-consistency analyses but names no statistical software or package used for the analyses.
gaps.importance: Limits reproducibility and software-use accounting for the analytic work.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record analysis software if reported in supplementary material or a corrigendum.

gaps.evidence: Participants compared the EQ-5D-5L alone with the EQ-5D-5L plus bolt-ons within the same interview, in addition to the between-group comparison of AD and CU samples.
gaps.importance: The within-person instrument comparison is a defining feature of the cognitive debriefing design but only one comparison value can be recorded on the axis.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow multiple comparison_structure values or an explicit secondary comparison key.
source: Results/Cognitive debriefing - relevance of the EQ-5D-5L and bolt-ons

gaps.evidence: The paper states 'We analyzed baseline data from a single-center longitudinal study conducted in Indonesia' with references to two companion papers, yet describes recruitment, instrument administration and data collection in first person as its own activity.
gaps.importance: Determines whether patient questionnaire data are CURRENT_STUDY_COLLECTION or PRIOR_RESEARCH_COLLECTION for the reported analysis.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer confirmation of whether the baseline survey is the current study's own collection or reuse of a separate parent study's data.
source: Methods > Study design and patients, para 1

gaps.evidence: 'The study survey was developed by the EQ-DAPHNIE Project Team using a modified Delphi method for selecting measures and variables' - an expert consensus procedure for selecting survey content that is neither data collection, analysis, nor stakeholder participatory design.
gaps.importance: Consensus-based selection of instruments and variables defines the survey content of the whole project.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider an EXPERT_CONSENSUS_OR_DELPHI method function value.

gaps.evidence: The paper describes rationale, design and data collection methods only; no statistical analysis plan for population health estimates or instrument comparison is reported beyond a mention of post-stratification weighting.
gaps.importance: Analysis methods determine how the stated aims of population health assessment and instrument evaluation will be met.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Extract analysis methods from subsequent EQ-DAPHNIE analysis publications.

gaps.evidence: The paper does not state the language of instrument administration for the US online survey.
gaps.importance: Minor; limits reproducibility of administration details.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record language if reported in the source publications of the parent study.

gaps.evidence: The EQ-5D Index is a value-set-derived score rather than an instrument as such; the review synthesises its measurement properties alongside the EQ VAS, and value sets used in included studies are extracted but not named.
gaps.importance: Affects whether the Index should be modelled as an instrument use or as an existing scoring product use.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer to decide whether EQ-5D Index evidence should be represented via a ProductUse of the underlying value sets when these are named in the supplementary extraction file.

gaps.evidence: Lung function tests (spirometry, carbon monoxide gas diffusion, 6 min walk distance) are objective physiological measurements rather than participant responses, qualitative material, aggregates, model parameters, simulated units or documents.
gaps.importance: Data level determines how objective clinical measurement data are represented for construct-validity analyses.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a data level value for objective clinical or physiological measurement.

gaps.evidence: Table 3 reports 'EQ-5D index (crosswalk)' without naming the country value set or crosswalk source used to derive the index.
gaps.importance: The exact value set determines the reported index score's interpretation and comparability.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Seek the exact crosswalk value set identity from the authors or the parent cohort publications.

gaps.evidence: The primary outcome is unconscious death thought accessibility measured by a word completion test, a psychological construct that is neither a health status, preference, behaviour, clinical event, service use, nor a measurement property.
gaps.importance: High: the study's primary outcome cannot be classified in the current outcome vocabulary.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider an outcome family for psychological or cognitive constructs studied as determinants of health valuation.

gaps.evidence: The mortality salience essay, the television control essay, the PANAS and the word puzzle are experimental manipulations or delay/filler tasks rather than data collection, analysis, or design construction activities.
gaps.importance: Medium: the functional role of manipulation and filler tasks is central to the experimental procedure but is not represented.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a method function for experimental manipulation or priming and for filler/delay procedures.
source: Methods > Positive and negative affect schedule (PANAS)

gaps.evidence: The survey was aborted for respondents with EQ-5D-5L anxiety/depression level 4 or higher, and the marketing bureau did not provide data on the number of respondents dropping out.
gaps.importance: Medium: exclusion and dropout counts are missing for the participant flow.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record the exclusion count if the authors report it elsewhere.

gaps.evidence: The study evaluates content validity of an experimental instrument (supporting MEASUREMENT_PROPERTY_EVALUATION) while being framed and titled as a stage in developing the EQ-TIPS instrument with recommended content changes for future versions (supporting INSTRUMENT_VERSION_DEVELOPMENT); no revised instrument version is produced in this paper.
gaps.importance: Determines the primary family assignment for a content-validity consultation within an ongoing instrument development programme.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer adjudication of whether expert content recommendations without a released revised version count as instrument content output.

gaps.evidence: 'Bolt-ons were selected using a symptom-guided, literature-based approach in line with current EQ-5D bolt-on recommendations [11].'
gaps.importance: The bolt-on selection procedure is a defining methodological step but no controlled method function covers candidate-domain selection.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a method function for candidate dimension or domain selection.

gaps.evidence: The paper states 'we conducted the second wave of the online survey' but also refers to 'the protocol for the original study' (Jumamyradov et al. child health valuation protocol), so the EQ-5D-5L and PROMIS-16 responses may be a secondary use of a parent valuation survey rather than a purpose-designed collection.
gaps.importance: Affects whether the data origin is CURRENT_STUDY_COLLECTION or PRIOR_RESEARCH_COLLECTION and the context of the survey-level protocol, sampling and task uses.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer confirmation of whether this psychometric comparison was a planned aim of the 2024 survey wave or a secondary analysis of the valuation survey data.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports only the analysed sample of 510 autistic children from the P-MIC study; recruitment, invitation and enrolment counts for the ASD cohort are not reported in this publication.
gaps.importance: Limits assessment of participation and attrition for the reused cohort.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consult the P-MIC study protocol and technical methods paper for the full recruitment flow.

gaps.evidence: The study compares SES groups within countries (BETWEEN_GROUP) and simultaneously compares six countries (BETWEEN_CONTEXT); only one value can be recorded on this axis.
gaps.importance: The cross-country comparison is a stated headline feature of the study ('a six-country comparison').
gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow more than one comparison_structure value or add a combined between-group-and-context value.

gaps.evidence: The Methods describe weighted linear regression, FIML estimation, predictive margins and violin/box plots, but no statistical software or package is named.
gaps.importance: Software identity is needed for reproducibility and for corpus-level software counts.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record software if reported in supplementary material or a corrigendum.

gaps.evidence: 'The ASCOT and EQ-5D-5L surveys were randomly assigned to participants while the QOL-ACC and EQ-HWB were fixed and QOL-ACC was just presented to participants who were 65 + age.'
gaps.importance: The source survey randomized instrument presentation, but the current secondary analysis makes no assignment, so the study-level allocation axis cannot record this source-study randomization.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow an allocation or presentation-order fact scoped to source-study data provenance.

gaps.evidence: Assessments were conducted at 11 European, 3 US and 17 European sites but the source does not report the instrument or interview languages used.
gaps.importance: Language versions matter for interpreting multinational EQ-5D-3L psychometric results.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record language versions if reported in the cohort source publications.
source: Patients and Methods > Study Design, Recruitment, and Sample

gaps.evidence: The "EQ-VT quality control (QC) tool" is described both as a tool generating fortnightly quality reports and as a quality control process focused on protocol compliance and face validity, so it could be modelled as a MethodUse, SoftwareUse, or a quality-control ProtocolUse.
gaps.importance: Affects the counting of quality-control software versus method use across valuation studies.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Registry review of the EQ-VT QC tool identity to fix its entity type.

gaps.evidence: The Van Hout et al. crosswalk algorithm was both applied to derive crosswalk value sets and examined as the object of the comparison; the product_function vocabulary has no value for an existing product applied as a derivation tool.
gaps.importance: Medium: the applied derivation role of the existing crosswalk product is not fully represented.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a product function for an existing product applied as an analytic or derivation tool.

gaps.evidence: The TTO data come from an ongoing project by the same author that 'was not designed to compare tele-TTO and personal TTO interviews' and 'aimed to replicate and extend the findings reported in Lipman and colleagues [32]', but the data are first reported here by the sole author who conducted all interviews.
gaps.importance: Determines whether the interview data are current-study collection or reuse of a separate project's research collection.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Reviewer to confirm whether the parent project constitutes a separate source study, in which case origin should become PRIOR_RESEARCH_COLLECTION with source-study contexts for collection, sampling and instrument uses.
source: Section 'Tele-TTO Applied in Practice', paragraphs 1 and 3

gaps.evidence: Participants completed 'a brief demographic questionnaire' whose results describe the sample, but no listed instrument function (predictor, outcome, content test, reference only) clearly fits a background characteristics form.
gaps.importance: Low; affects only classification of a descriptive background instrument.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add or confirm a function value for background/characteristics collection instruments.

gaps.evidence: The PAS-Cog score was used by facilities to determine residents' cognitive functioning and eligibility to participate in interviews, not to measure a study outcome, predictor, or health state.
gaps.importance: Eligibility-screening use of an instrument cannot be represented exactly with the available instrument_function values.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add an instrument function for eligibility screening or participant selection.
source: Aim and Methods > Interview Recruitment and Procedure

gaps.evidence: The EQ-VT quality control software performs real-time monitoring of protocol compliance and interviewer performance, a quality-control function that no software_function value covers exactly; DATA_MANAGEMENT was used as the closest value.
gaps.importance: Quality control software is a defining component of EQ-VT version 2 and is likely recurrent across valuation studies.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider adding a QUALITY_CONTROL software function value.
source: Sect. 'The EQ-VT Protocol'; Table 1 row 'Quality control'

gaps.evidence: The study simultaneously compares two instruments (3L vs 5L) and 14 country-specific value sets across seven countries, so both BETWEEN_INSTRUMENT and BETWEEN_CONTEXT plausibly apply on the single comparison axis.
gaps.importance: Medium: the country comparison is an explicit analytic dimension (country as regression covariate, inter-country differences reported).
gaps.proposed_resolution: Allow a secondary comparison value or record the country comparison through StudyFactor 'Country of value set'.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports search strategy, selection criteria and appraisal but names no registered review protocol or reporting guideline (e.g. PRISMA) for the review itself.
gaps.importance: Limits assessment of review conduct against prespecified methods.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Confirm from supplementary material whether a review protocol or reporting guideline was used.
source: Methods > Data Sources, Search Strategy, Study Selection, and Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria

gaps.evidence: The published Dutch 3L and 5L tariffs were used as rescaling anchors for the DC values, not strictly as analysis objects or comparators.
gaps.importance: Affects the exact functional role of an existing value set within a valuation study.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a product function value for anchoring or rescaling reference.
source: Methods > Analysis > EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L Values and Value' Distributions

gaps.evidence: The paper reports a Dutch general population online survey but does not state the language of the instrument or survey.
gaps.importance: Language of the descriptive system is central to the paper's own phrasing argument.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Seek language information from the survey materials or authors.

gaps.evidence: The conditional logit model was used to optimize the experimental design rather than to report results, and footnote 2 explains why mixed logit was preferred for estimation; no listed analytic role exactly covers a design-optimization model.
gaps.importance: Medium; affects how the design-stage model is counted in analytic-role aggregates.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider an analytic role for a model used only in experimental-design optimization.
source: Methods > Experimental Designs With/Without Severity-Stratified Restriction

gaps.evidence: The study compares three existing/new value sets (EQ-5D-5L directly measured, EQ-5D-5L cross-walk, EQ-5D-3L), which is a comparison between value-set products rather than between groups, methods, instruments or contexts.
gaps.importance: Affects design classification of the value-set comparison component.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a BETWEEN_PRODUCT comparison_structure value for value-set comparisons.

gaps.evidence: The Excel-based quality-control tool enables monitoring of protocol compliance, interviewer effects and validity of the collected data; no quality-control software function exists, so DATA_MANAGEMENT was used.
gaps.importance: Understates the quality-control role of the tool.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider a QUALITY_CONTROL software function.

gaps.evidence: 'Given a planned experimental arm of our research... (the methods and results of the experimental substudy will be reported elsewhere)' and 'After excluding interviews with experimental TTO blocks (the results of the study will be reported elsewhere)'.
gaps.importance: The experimental arm contributed to total interviews but its design, sample and results are not reported here.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Link to the separate publication reporting the experimental substudy when available.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports a pilot test of 10 interviews per interviewer for the first group of 15 interviewers, but does not state how many pilot interviews were conducted or whether they were included in the 1143 interviews used for the main analysis.
gaps.importance: Affects the separation of pilot and formal data collection samples.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Seek clarification of pilot interview counts and their inclusion in the analysed dataset.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports 1210 DCE respondents as a denominator and 1276 adults obtained from the panel, but does not report the number invited or approached in the online panel.
gaps.importance: Limits assessment of DCE response and exclusion flow.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Obtain panel invitation and response counts from the authors.

gaps.evidence: The study applies published utility algorithms to exhaustively enumerated theoretical health states rather than collecting empirical observations; MODEL_BASED and QUANTITATIVE_EMPIRICAL both remain plausible.
gaps.importance: Affects design classification of a computational value-set comparison.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Review whether exhaustive computation of theoretical values from published value-set models should default to MODEL_BASED.

gaps.evidence: Table 2 reports EQ-5D-5L index values (mean 0.8 for cTTO sample, 0.9 for DCE sample) but the paper does not name the value set or scoring algorithm used to derive them.
gaps.importance: The scoring product applied to EQ-5D-5L responses cannot be identified.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record the exact value set used to compute EQ-5D-5L index values.

gaps.evidence: Footnote 3 states that the interviews also contained 15 DCE tasks addressing a research objective outside the scope of this paper, and these data are not considered further.
gaps.importance: A data-collection component of the interviews yields no reported result in this publication.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Link the add-on DCE component to the publication that reports its results.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports statistical analyses and bootstrapping and states 'The code however is available upon request', but names no statistical software or package.
gaps.importance: Analytic reproducibility and software-use coverage of the corpus.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record no SoftwareUse item; request software identity from authors if needed.

gaps.evidence: SF-36 item 1, mRS and Barthel Index serve as external anchors classifying change; the vocabulary has no 'anchor' instrument function, so COMPARATOR was used.
gaps.importance: Anchor-based responsiveness designs recur across the corpus.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider an explicit external-anchor instrument function.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports face-to-face paper-based DCE interviews in Indonesia but does not state the language of the instrument or interview.
gaps.importance: Language version matters for an EQ-5D-Y-3L valuation study in a multilingual country.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave language fields empty until the source reports them.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports mixed-logit and mapping model estimation but names no statistical software; Code Availability states 'Not applicable'.
gaps.importance: Analysis software is a routine reproducibility fact for value-set estimation.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Record no analysis SoftwareUse for this study.

gaps.evidence: The reported outcomes are stakeholders' normative views and methodological recommendations on youth valuation, which fit no exact outcome family; CONCEPTUAL_CLASSIFICATION was the closest available value.
gaps.importance: Affects comparability of outcome-family counts for stakeholder-engagement studies.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Consider an outcome family for stakeholder or expert normative input on method design.
source: Results, paragraphs 3 and following; VOCABULARY outcome_family list

gaps.evidence: The interview included 'an additional DCE survey trying to determine the value of QALYs in Slovenia', but no design detail, analysis, or result for this component is reported in this paper.
gaps.importance: Moderate: an add-on data-collection component of the same interview whose data are not reported here.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Link to the separate publication reporting the QALY-value DCE when identified.

gaps.evidence: The main text states only that ‘the value sets used for these analyses are available in Supplementary Table S10’ for the EQ-5D-Y-3L, CHU9D, AQoL-6D and HUI3; exact value-set identities are not given in the article text.
gaps.importance: Prevents exact identification of the value sets applied in the utility-score sensitivity analyses.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Retrieve exact value-set identities from ESM Table S10 during registry review.

gaps.evidence: The a priori consensus method by which the study team specified convergent and divergent item-pair hypotheses is a hypothesis-specification procedure that could map to MEASUREMENT_PROPERTY_ANALYSIS or QUALITY_CONTROL.
gaps.importance: Affects classification of a defining step in the convergent/divergent validity analysis.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Review whether hypothesis specification for construct validity should have a dedicated method function.

gaps.evidence: The Chinese national COVID-19 diagnosis and treatment protocol (Trial Version 10) was used to classify paediatric COVID-19 severity and recovery, but it does not govern the study, valuation, translation, quality control, reporting, or appraisal.
gaps.importance: The severity and recovery classifications define the known-groups and responsiveness criteria.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Add a clinical classification or case-definition protocol function.

gaps.evidence: The paper reports that all value sets for seven generic instruments were identified and plotted in Fig. 1, but no numeric count of identified value sets is given in the text.
gaps.importance: Prevents recording the size of the desktop review inventory that underpins the chronological finding.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Leave the identified-value-set count unrecorded unless a count is added from the figure data.

gaps.evidence: The article is labelled a 'Current Opinion' by the journal but its principal output is a developed taxonomy with evidence requirements and solutions, fitting either OPINION_ARTICLE or CONCEPTUAL_ARTICLE.
gaps.importance: Affects publication-form counting for opinion versus conceptual outputs.
gaps.proposed_resolution: Mapped to CONCEPTUAL_ARTICLE because a taxonomy/framework is the principal output; flag for reviewer confirmation.
source: Abstract ('In this Current Opinion, we develop a taxonomy of value set obsolescence')

gaps.evidence: The data collection had no planned group, instrument, or method comparison, but the study's central analysis compares six competing model specifications with and without heteroskedasticity adjustment via cross-validation.
gaps.importance: Affects whether the comparison axis should be NONCOMPARATIVE or a comparison value for competing statistical models.
